meta.title: OpenAEC BCF Manager Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: BCF Manager Studio: open source web platform for BIM issues following the open BCF 2.1 standard. Issues, comments and viewpoints per project, a full BCF API 2.1 server and BCF file import and export. Self-hosted with Docker.

header.label: In development · BIM issue management
header.title: BCF Manager Studio
header.tagline: Manage BIM issues with the open BCF standard
header.desc: Report, discuss and track problems in a building model, with viewpoints, comments and assignment per project. BCF Manager Studio is a web platform with a full BCF API 2.1 server that you run on your own server with Docker. Your data stays yours.

alt.dashboard: Project dashboard of BCF Manager Studio with the issues by status and priority
alt.issue: An issue with viewpoint, description and comments
alt.issues: The issue list with status, priority and assignee

notice.text: Not production-ready yet: this tool is in development. You can try it out, but do not use it for real project work yet. Report what you run into on GitHub.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From report to resolution
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

issues.title: Every problem in one place
issues.desc: An issue follows the BCF 2.1 standard: a title and description, a status and priority, an assignee, a due date and labels. Comments stay with the issue, so the whole discussion can be read back.

viewpoints.title: See what is meant
viewpoints.desc: A viewpoint records the camera, the selection, the visibility and a snapshot of the model. Through the GlobalId a BCF viewer jumps straight to the right IFC element.

dashboard.title: An overview per project
dashboard.desc: Every project has its own dashboard with the open issues by status and priority. Filter by labels, stages and assignees, and see at a glance where things are stuck.

host.title: On your own server, in your own cloud
host.desc: Start the platform with Docker Compose. Users sign in through single sign-on, and the issues of each project can live in your own Nextcloud, next to the IFC models. Several organizations share one installation.

topics.title: BCF 2.1 issues
topics.desc: Create, edit and close issues following the BCF 2.1 standard.

comments.title: Comments
comments.desc: The discussion per issue, with author and date.

assign.title: Assignment and due dates
assign.desc: Assign an issue to a team member and follow its status until it is resolved.

labels.title: Labels, priorities and stages
labels.desc: Your own lists per project, with default values for a new project.

events.title: Change log
events.desc: Every change to an issue or project is recorded.

viewpoints.title: Viewpoints with a snapshot
viewpoints.desc: Camera, selection and visibility of the model, with a snapshot for every issue.

ifc.title: IFC link
ifc.desc: Issues refer to elements in the IFC model through their GlobalId.

xml.title: BCF files
xml.desc: Import a BCF file by dragging it into the window, and export to any package that supports BCF.

api.title: BCF API 2.1
api.desc: All 29 endpoints of the standard, so BCF software can talk to the platform directly.

keys.title: API keys per project
keys.desc: Let other tools and scripts read and write issues without signing in.

selfhosted.title: Self-hosted
selfhosted.desc: Run everything on your own server with Docker Compose. No vendor cloud.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.desc: Sign in through OpenID Connect; new users are created automatically the first time.

cloud.title: Storage in Nextcloud
cloud.desc: Keep the issues per project in your own Nextcloud, next to the IFC models.

tenants.title: Several organizations
tenants.desc: One installation for several organizations, each with its own storage.

whatsnew.label: Latest developments
whatsnew.title: The full BCF API and storage in your own cloud
whatsnew.desc: There is no release yet. This was added to the source code in the spring of 2026.

api.title: BCF API 2.1 complete
api.desc: Versions, authentication, extensions, viewpoint components and events: all 29 endpoints work.

cloud.title: Storage in Nextcloud
cloud.desc: Issues per project next to the IFC models, with a project manifest that is updated on every save.

auth.title: Sign in through your organization
auth.desc: Single sign-on with Authentik, and service tokens for connections between apps.

tenants.title: Several organizations
tenants.desc: One installation serves several organizations, each with its own storage and its own allowed addresses.

status.q: Can I use BCF Manager Studio yet?
status.a: Not as a ready-made app: there is no release and no public demo yet. If you want to try it, start the platform with Docker Compose on a server of your own; the source code is on GitHub.

cost.a: Nothing. The source code is free to use under the MIT license. You only pay for the server you run the platform on.

bcf.a: The BIM Collaboration Format is an open buildingSMART standard for exchanging issues and comments about a building model, as a file (XML in a zip) or through a REST API. It lets you discuss problems in a model, whatever software each party uses.

software.q: Does it work with my BIM software?
software.a: With any package that supports BCF 2.1: through BCF files that you import and export, or directly through the BCF API 2.1.

data.a: On your own server, in a PostgreSQL database. If you like, the platform keeps the issues per project in your own Nextcloud, next to the IFC models. There is no vendor cloud in between.

login.a: Through single sign-on with OpenID Connect, for example with Authentik. Other tools and scripts connect with an API key per project.

lang.q: What language is the app in?
lang.a: The interface is in Dutch for now. A choice between Dutch and English is planned.

validator.q: How does it work with the BIM Validator?
validator.a: The BIM Validator checks IFC models and turns its findings into BCF issues. You import those as a BCF file. A direct connection through API keys is planned.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: One Docker Compose file starts the database, the server and the web interface.

rust.title: Rust and Axum
rust.desc: A fast, memory-safe server for the BCF API and the web interface.

db.title: PostgreSQL
db.desc: Projects, issues, comments and viewpoints in a reliable database.

react.title: React and TypeScript
react.desc: The web interface with ribbon and Backstage in the OpenAEC house style.

bcf.title: BCF 2.1 and BCF API 2.1
bcf.desc: The open buildingSMART standards, for files and for the REST API.

oidc.title: OpenID Connect
oidc.desc: Sign in through your organization's identity service.

docker.title: Docker and Caddy
docker.desc: Containers for the whole installation, with Caddy as the web server in front.
